stories.title: Anwar says a global investor plans US$50b tech investment in Malaysia
stories.summary: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim on Saturday disclosed that a global investor plans to invest US$50 billion (RM204 billion) in the artificial intelligence (AI), new technology and data centre sectors in Sarawak and Peninsular Malaysia.
stories.why_it_matters: If this commitment materialises, it would significantly accelerate Malaysia's emergence as a hyperscale and AI data centre hub, adding to the wave of capacity announced across Johor and the Klang Valley. Sarawak's inclusion signals that data centre development is spreading beyond the traditional southern corridor, with implications for power demand, land pricing and competition for renewable energy across both regions. The lack of a named investor, however, means the announcement should be treated as aspirational until contracts are signed.

sources.name: The Edge Malaysia — data centre search

stories.content:
MELAKA (Oct 24): Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim on Saturday disclosed that a global investor plans to invest US$50 billion (RM204 billion) in the artificial intelligence (AI), new technology and data centre sectors in Sarawak and Peninsular Malaysia.

He said the investor conveyed the intention during a recent video conference with him, describing the proposed investment as one of the largest in the region.

Anwar said this technology sector investment can create new and better job opportunities for Malaysians, particularly the younger generation, including students in schools and institutions of higher learning.

“Last Tuesday, one of the world’s largest investors held a video conference with me. The investor said he had chosen Kuching, Sarawak, and Peninsular Malaysia for an investment worth US$50 billion, one of the largest investments in the region.

“In which sectors? AI, new technology and data centres. This means that young people currently studying at universities and in schools must recognise that there will be new opportunities waiting, including better employment opportunities,” he said.

Anwar was speaking at the Sentuhan Kasih Madani Programme and launch of the National Cost of Living Action Plan 2030, held at the Hang Jebat Sports Complex here on Saturday. Also at the event was Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Minister Datuk Armizan Mohd Ali.

The prime minister said international investors’ confidence in Malaysia must be maintained through the country’s political stability and leadership, as well as by ensuring a conducive environment for investment.

Anwar cited peace and harmony among Malaysia’s multiracial and multireligious communities as being one of the country’s strengths, saying it should be leveraged to attract more foreign investment.

“If people don’t have confidence in this government, and if the leadership is constantly quarrelling, investors will not be interested in coming here,” he said.

Meanwhile, Anwar said, Malaysia must continue strengthening its capabilities in emerging technologies, particularly AI, digitalisation and semiconductors, to ensure sustainable economic growth.

He said efforts to enhance workforce training and skills development are also crucial to enable Malaysia to move beyond back-end technology activities into the middle- and front-end segments, which offer higher added value.

However, Anwar stressed that the success in attracting investments and drive economic growth needs to be translated into real benefits for the people, including better job opportunities and higher standard of living.

stories.title_zh: Anwar：一家全球投资者计划在马来西亚投资500亿美元用于科技领域
stories.summary_zh: 首相拿督斯里安华·依布拉欣（Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim）周六透露，一家全球投资者计划在马来西亚砂拉越和半岛地区的人工智能（AI）、新技术和数据中心领域投资500亿美元（2040亿令吉）。
stories.why_zh: 如果这一承诺得以落实，将显著加速马来西亚成为 hyperscale 和 AI 数据中心枢纽的进程，为柔佛和巴生谷地区已宣布的一波容量建设再添助力。沙捞越的加入表明数据中心开发正在向传统南部走廊以外扩展，这对两个地区的电力需求、土地定价以及可再生能源竞争都将产生影响。然而，由于尚未公布投资者名称，在该公告落实为正式合同之前，应将其视为一种愿景性表态。
